newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post front page - May 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post front page - May 14.

text.p: The Washington Post carried the following stories on its front page on May 14:

WASHINGTON - The White House signalled that President Clinton could support a Democratic bill to curtail late-term abortions in hopes of derailing a Republican proposal to outlaw "partial birth" abortions.
WASHINGTON - The District's cable television provider is in a sad state with unfilled orders, piracy, billing errors, poor service and lousy reception plaguing its operations.

KINSHASA, Zaire - On the eve of talks aimed at ending Zaire's seven-month-old conflict, a siege mentality settled over the capital as the government imposed a curfew, issued a shoot-to-kill order against looters and called for residents to help defend the city from a potential rebel onslaught.

WASHINGTON - The Pentagon opened a formal review this week into allegations by gay rights advocates that military investigators are wrongfully conducting aggressive inquiries into the sex lives of gay service members.
PARIS - All French students carry the burden of this country's academic traditions: rigorous study of the classical disciplines, long school days in austere surroundings, and hours of homework.

HONG KONG - Forty-eight days from now Britain will hand Hong Kong back to China, but the young dealmakers and investment bankers who gather in bars along Lan Kwai Fong Street on Friday nights predict a happy marriage of markets and financial muscle.
NEW YORK - A Danish actress was arrested for leaving her 14-month-old infant in a stroller outside a New York restaurant, a common practice in Copenhagen.
